title: Get Up With It
desc_lfm_album: Get Up With It is a double album by American jazz trumpeter Miles Davis, released in 1974 on Columbia Records. It is a dense and sprawling work primarily composed of recordings from 1970 to 1974, showcasing Davis's evolving electric jazz fusion sound and his deepening exploration of funk, rock, and avant-garde elements. The album is notable for its extended track lengths, its incorporation of diverse musical textures, and its status as a bridge between the more explicitly rock-influenced *On the Corner* and the introspective *Agharta* and *Pangaea*. "Mothership Connection" became Parliament's first album to be certified gold and later platinum. .

title: Sextant
desc_lfm_album: Herbie Hancock's Sextant, released on March 30, 1973, stands as an album that redefined the boundaries of jazz fusion. This groundbreaking work emerged during a transformative period in jazz history, when traditional acoustic instruments were being augmented by electronic innovations. desc_lfm_album: Electric Circus is the fifth studio album by rapper Common, released December 10, 2002 on the now-defunct MCA Records. The album was highly anticipated and praised by many critics for its ambitious vision. In March 2015 she released her debut album Dark Energy on Planet Mu.
